explanations.explanation: You got it, baker! Paul tells them, "Stand firm, then, and do not be encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery" (Galatians 5:1). They did not have to earn it, because Christ already paid the price.

explanations.answer: Work hard to earn their freedom
explanations.explanation: No, baker, they cannot earn what has already been given. Paul says, "It is for freedom that Christ has set us free" (Galatians 5:1). Trying to earn it is like trying to pay a debt that's already been completely wiped out.
Not quite! Paul does not want them hiding in the corner. He tells them to "Stand firm" in the freedom Christ has given them, and not let anyone drag them back into slavery (Galatians 5:1).
That is true! Paul warns them, "do not be encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery" (Galatians 5:1). He does not want them trading their clean, beautiful freedom for heavy iron chains.

Actually, it is true, baker! Paul warns them, "do not be encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery" (Galatians 5:1). He is pleading with them to keep those heavy, legalistic chains far away from their necks.

Perfect bake! Paul writes, "if you let yourselves be circumcised, Christ will be of no value to you at all" (Galatians 5:2). Trying to add human effort to His perfect work completely cancels out the gift of grace.
No, baker. Trying to add circumcision to make Christ's work "better" actually does the opposite. Paul says that if they do this, "Christ will be of no value to you at all" (Galatians 5:2).
Not at all, baker! Paul does not say it makes no difference. He warns them that if they turn to circumcision to save them, "Christ will be of no value to you at all" (Galatians 5:2).

Actually, this is false! Paul says the exact opposite. He testifies that if a man gets circumcised to keep the law, "he is obligated to obey the whole law" (Galatians 5:3). You cannot just pick and choose the easy rules, baker!

You are right, baker! Paul warns that if a man gets circumcised under the law, "he is obligated to obey the whole law" (Galatians 5:3). If you want to use the law to save you, you have to keep every single speck of it perfectly.

explanations.answer: They have been severed from Christ
explanations.explanation: That is the right bake! Paul says, "You who are trying to be justified by the law have been severed from Christ; you have fallen away from grace" (Galatians 5:4). It is a terrifying picture, like cutting yourself off from the only branch that gives life.

explanations.answer: They have drawn closer to Christ
explanations.explanation: No, it is the exact opposite! Paul warns, "You who are trying to be justified by the law have been severed from Christ" (Galatians 5:4). Turning back to the law for salvation actually cuts you off from Him.

No, baker. You cannot earn grace by works. Paul warns those trying to be justified by the law that they "have fallen away from grace" (Galatians 5:4). Trying to earn grace is like trying to pay for a free gift.
You got it, friend! Paul says, "But by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness" (Galatians 5:5). We do not wait on our own perfect performance; we trust in Him by faith.
No, baker. The law cannot bring righteousness. Paul says it is "by faith" that they eagerly await the hope of righteousness through the Spirit (Galatians 5:5).
Not human effort, baker! Paul points them right back to trust. He says that "by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness" (Galatians 5:5).

That's a keeper! Paul says that in Christ Jesus, "What matters is faith expressing itself through love" (Galatians 5:6). True faith doesn't sit still like raw flour; it gets to work and pours itself out in love for others.
No, baker. Paul has been showing them that trying to keep the law to save themselves only cuts them off from Christ. What matters in Him is "faith expressing itself through love" (Galatians 5:6).

explanations.answer: Coming from the right family line
explanations.explanation: Not at all! Paul says that external things like circumcision mean nothing. In Christ Jesus, "What matters is faith expressing itself through love" (Galatians 5:6).

Actually, this is false! Paul says, "Such persuasion does not come from the One who calls you" (Galatians 5:8). God called them to freedom, so any voice telling them to go back to slavery is not from Him!

You are right, baker! Paul says, "Such persuasion does not come from the One who calls you" (Galatians5:8). God is the One who set them free, so He is certainly not the One trying to lock them back up in rules.

Perfect bake! Paul says, "A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough" (Galatians 5:9). Just like a tiny pinch of yeast spreads through the entire bowl of flour, a small bit of false teaching can corrupt a whole church.
No, baker. Anyone who has ever made bread knows yeast doesn't stay in one spot! Paul says, "A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough" (Galatians 5:9).
No, baker! Leaven is sneaky and powerful. Paul says, "A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough" (Galatians 5:9). You cannot let even a little bit of false legalism slide into the mix.

Fine work, baker! Paul says, "The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be" (Galatians 5:10). Anyone who tries to drag God's people back into legalistic slavery has a heavy day of judgment coming.

explanations.answer: He will be let off free
explanations.explanation: No, baker. Paul is very serious about people who corrupt the gospel. He says, "The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be" (Galatians 5:10).

explanations.answer: He will be put in charge
explanations.explanation: Absolutely not! Paul has no intention of letting this troublemaker lead. He warns that "The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be" (Galatians 5:10).

Actually, this is false! Paul is making a point by showing how ridiculous that idea is. He says that if he were still preaching circumcision, he wouldn't be persecuted anymore (Galatians 5:11). He does not preach it!

You got it, baker! Paul is showing how absurd that rumor is. He asks, "if I am still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted?" (Galatians 5:11). He stands firmly for salvation by grace alone.
That is true, baker! Paul warns them, "do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh" (Galatians 5:13). Freedom from the law does not mean a free pass to do whatever selfish things we want!
Actually, it is true! Paul tells them, "do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh" (Galatians 5:13). Christian freedom is not a license to go wild with selfish desires.

Box-worthy! Paul writes, "The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree: 'Love your neighbor as yourself'" (Galatians 5:14). If you want to keep the heart of God's commands, you start by loving the folks right next to you.
No, baker. While that is a commandment, Paul says the *entire* law is summarized and fulfilled in this one decree: "Love your neighbor as yourself" (Galatians 5:14).
Not this one, baker. Paul points them to the ultimate summary of the law. He says, "The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree: 'Love your neighbor as yourself'" (Galatians 5:14).

That is the right bake! Paul warns, "But if you keep on biting and devouring one another, watch out, or you will be consumed by one another" (Galatians 5:15). If we treat each other like wild animals, we'll end up destroying the whole flock!
Not scattered, baker! Paul uses a much more vivid and dangerous picture. He says that if they keep biting and devouring, they will be "consumed" by one another (Galatians 5:15).
No, baker. Paul says they will be "consumed by one another" (Galatians 5:15). Infighting and bickering do not just hurt feelings; they can eat a whole community alive.
